messages.subject: Re: How to move from CFA (measEq.syntax) to SEM with invariance constraints
parts: how do I transition from the measurement invariance model to the structural model, given that measEq.syntax is designed for CFA models, and the argument ID.cat = "Wu.Estabrook.2016" is not applicable in sem?

The same identification methods are applicable to any SEM, not only to a CFA with exogenous factors.  But note that you can only apply constraints to a factor's residual variance, not marginal variance.  In a CFA, there is no distinction because the factors are exogenous (no predictors, so residual variance is total/marginal variance).  

To transition to a structural model from the invariance syntax provided by semTools::measEq.syntax(), you can copy the as.character() output to a syntax file and edit the section ## COMMON-FACTOR COVARIANCES by deleting any (residual) covariances that should not be estimated in your structural model.  Obviously, you also need to add the structural regression paths to the lavaan syntax.
since parameterization = "theta" is recommended for measurement models with ordinal data
That is only necessary if you wish to evaluate strict invariance.
should I retain this parameterization when specifying the structural model, or is it advisable to switch to parameterization = "delta" at that stage?

If you are not imposing strict-invariance constraints on indicators' residual variances, then it is arbitrary whether you choose delta or theta parameterization.
